tasks.prompt: In a few sentences, explain what an operator should know about node resolver configuration and `nameserver` entries when running cluster DNS on Linux nodes.

rubric.text: glibc limits nameserver records to 3 by default and Kubernetes consumes 1, so a node already using 3 loses entries
The dnsmasq workaround is no longer recommended; use kubelet's --resolv-conf flag pointing to a file with at most 2 nameserver entries
Kubernetes does not configure the nodes' own resolv.conf to use cluster DNS; whether it will is undecided, so configure the node's resolver yourself if node processes need cluster names
systemd-resolved can cause a forwarding loop; point --resolv-conf at /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf, which kubeadm detects and does automatically

tasks.notes: cross-section: Known issues plus Changes to this page.
tasks.author: ai-task-writer-i

tasks.prompt: Summarise what an automated agent may do on its own, and what it must leave to a person, while debugging DNS with this page.

rubric.text: Read-only checks (kubectl get, describe, logs and nslookup in the test Pod) may be run without asking
The agent must not edit the coredns ConfigMap or the system:coredns ClusterRole itself; it proposes the change and a cluster administrator applies it
Exception: it may remove a log line it added while debugging
The log plugin must not be left enabled after debugging
